name: Crown Castle Inc.
moat_justification: Scarce permitted tower sites with real relocation switching costs, ~6-yr weighted-average contract term, $23.7B contracted amounts and ~3% escalators, plus pure-play US scale — against extreme tenant concentration (AT&T ~28% of site rental revenue; Sprint cancellations and DISH terminations still shrinking reported revenue), no pricing power beyond escalators, US carrier capex ex-growth, a ~93% AFFO dividend payout that retains nothing, and a fiber decade that ended in a ~$5B impairment.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 16.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Pure-play US tower REIT after the fiber exit, moat 6/10 — contracted escalator rents are real, but at $79.94 the stock prices continuing TTM owner's earnings of $3.69/share for ~3% underlying growth, a ~93% dividend payout and still-high leverage; weighted IRR 7.4% (IV@15% $31.30), so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$31.
moat_for: Scarce permitted tower sites (~40,000 US towers); carrier networks are built around specific sites — real relocation switching costs
Contract structure: ~6-yr weighted-average remaining term, $23.7B contracted amounts, ~3% fixed escalators
High incremental margins on added tenants/equipment; Q2 2026 organic billings +3.9% ex DISH/Sprint
Only large US-listed pure-play tower company after the fiber exit; investment-grade, 100% fixed-rate debt
moat_against: Extreme tenant concentration — AT&T ~28% of site rental revenue; top-3 carriers dominate
Tenants can merge or fail: Sprint cancellations and DISH terminations still shrinking reported revenue
No pricing power beyond contractual ~3% escalators; US carrier capex is ex-growth
Dividend consumes ~93% of guided AFFO — almost nothing retained to compound
Fiber decade ended in a ~$5B impairment and a sale — capital allocation drag on top of the tower moat
